issue.title: local variable messes up async result (goto loop vs. scope of captured variable)

system_prompt: You are a helpful AI assistant who classifies GitHub issues according to predefined categories. Your goal is to determine if the GitHub issue can be reproduced to verify the provided solution's correctness.
llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue can be analyzed without needing a build environment. The problem is a classic closure capture issue in C# with async code and goto statements. When using goto to loop back, the same 'result' variable is being reused, but the inner Task.Run captures this variable by reference, not by value. By the time some of the inner tasks execute, the outer loop may have already changed the value of 'result'. This is a conceptual programming issue that can be verified through code analysis without needing to build and run the code. The solution would involve properly scoping the variable (e.g., by creating a new local copy inside the loop) or restructuring the code to use a proper loop construct instead of goto. This is a pure language behavior issue that can be analyzed statically.
